sections.facts: Appellant Company filed criminal complaints under Section 630(1)(b) of the Companies Act and Section 406 of the IPC against its employees (the first respondent of each appeal) as they did not vacate the company quarters after about six months even after retirement. The Judicial Magistrate, First Class dismissed the complaints on the ground that they were not filed within the period of limitation of six months from the date of retirement of the respondent employees. The High Court, holding that the offence under Section 630(1) was not a continuing offence, dismissed the Company's revision petitions.
sections.statute: Section 630 and Section 630(1)(b) of the Companies Act; Section 406 of the Indian Penal Code; Section 473 and Chapter XXXVI of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
sections.analysis:
The beneficent provision contained in Section 630, no doubt penal, has been purposely enacted by the legislature with the object of providing a summary procedure for retrieving the property of the company: (a) where an officer or employee of a company wrongfully obtains possession of property of the company, or (b) where having been placed in possession of any such property during the course of his employment, wrongfully withholds possession of it after the termination of his employment. It is the duty of the court to place a broad and liberal construction on the provision in furtherance of the object and purpose of the legislation which would suppress the mischief and advance the remedy. 'Officer' or 'employee' in Section 630 of the Companies Act includes both present and past officers and employees.

The expression 'continuing offence' has not been defined in the Code. The question whether a particular offence is a 'continuing offence' or not must necessarily depend upon the language of the statute which creates that offence, the nature of the offence and the purpose intended to be achieved by constituting the particular act as an offence. The concept of continuing offence does not wipe out the original guilt, but it keeps the contravention alive day by day. Courts when confronted with provisions which lay down a rule of limitation governing prosecutions should give due weight and consideration to Section 473 of the Code, an overriding provision enabling cognizance after expiry of limitation if necessary in the interest of justice.

The offence under Section 630 is not such as can be said to have consummated once for all. Wrongful withholding, wrongfully obtaining possession, or wrongful application of the company's property cannot be said to be terminated by a single act or fact, but subsists for the period until the property is delivered up or refunded. It is an offence committed over a span of time where the last act controls the commencement of limitation; it consists of a continuous series of acts enduring after the period of consummation on refusal to deliver up the property. It is not an instantaneous offence and limitation begins with the cessation of the criminal act. The offence continues until the property is delivered up or refunded, for failure of which subsection (2) prescribes punishment. Thus, the offence under Section 630 is a continuing offence and limitation must be computed accordingly.
sections.judgement: Appeals of the Appellant Company allowed. The complaints could not be said to have been barred by limitation. (W.M.I. Cranes Ltd. vs G.G. Advani & Anr. overruled).
